value.rationale: The optimal constant for mean-zero data on the simplest graph with a free boundary is an intrinsic sharp stability invariant. The all-length monotonicity and explicit square-root deficit are not generic Poincare bounds: they isolate a boundary-driven extremizing scale \(x_N\sim\sqrt{2/N}\), quantify how far a finite graph is from its one-sided infinite lattice, and supply all equality configurations. The N^-1/2 law is qualitatively distinct from periodic finite-size behavior, making the exact normalization and coefficient useful in discrete trace and numerical stability analysis.
